items.title: Jane Fraser Set a New Course for Citigroup. It’s Working for Customers—and Investors.
items.summary: Jane Fraser isn’t the first CEO to try to turn around  Citigroup  But she might be the first to succeed where others have stalled.  Under her leadership, the bank has shed some overseas banking units, cut costs, and restructured its strategy around five units: services, markets, banking, consumer cards, and wealth.  Fraser, 58, has recruited talent from competitors to help spearhead her strategy.

items.title: Chip Maker AMD Has Become a Data-Center Powerhouse. It’s All Part of Lisa Su’s Plan.
items.summary: Lisa Su turned  Advanced Micro Devices  into the Comeback Kid of tech.  Before she took the reins in 2014, the chip maker was a perennial also-ran, lagging behind competitors  Nvidia  and  Intel  But since her first full year as CEO in 2015, sales have grown at a 24% annual rate—and by 38% in the most recent quarter.  Where once AMD chips were the second choice, they are now competitive in the data-center arena, the fastest-growing semiconductor market.

items.title: Darren Woods’ Game Plan at Exxon Mobil: Produce More Oil for Less Money
items.summary: Exxon Mobil  annual production just hit its highest level in over 40 years, allowing the company to play a central role in supplying the world with oil during the Iran war.  CEO Darren Woods’ decision to ramp up output in locations as diverse as Guyana, Texas, and Papua New Guinea has also paid off for shareholders.  Woods told investors in May he is proud to have kept his “pedal to the metal.”
